This project is designed to be installed directly from a git URL (`npm install -g <git url>`), and npm's global-install path is fragile: if package.json declares any of `preinstall`, `install`, `postinstall`, `prepare`, `prepack`, or `build`, npm triggers a nested install inside the cloned repo that inherits the outer `--global`/`--prefix` flags and corrupts the tree being installed. Committing the compiled `dist/` sidesteps that nested-install trap entirely, since no build step is needed at install time (CI verifies `dist/` stays in sync with source on every change). The current build script is deliberately named `compile` instead of `build` to avoid tripping this.

SCRIPTS: preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare, prepack, build

The check is `isProjectPath`, defined in `src/core/manifest.ts` (line 42-46).

It's called from `readManifest` (same file, line 66), which filters out any manifest entry whose `path` fails `isProjectPath` — i.e. is absolute, drive-letter-rooted, or resolves outside `cwd` via `..`. Since `sync.ts`'s deletion loop (`src/commands/sync.ts:128-141`) only ever iterates over entries that came from `readManifest`, an entry like `../secret.txt` is dropped before it ever reaches the `rmSync(abs)` call — so it can't be used to delete files outside the project.

Because `bin` points at `./dist/cli.js` and the package has no `postinstall`/`prepare` step, npm install (including installs straight from the git repo, which this local-first tool supports) must produce a working `cli.js` immediately without needing devDependencies like `typescript` present. Committing `dist/` guarantees the binary works right after checkout/install; `compile` only runs manually or via `prepublishOnly` when cutting an npm release, not on consumer install.

SCRIPTS: postinstall, prepare

The check is `isProjectPath` in `src/core/manifest.ts` (lines 42–46).

`readManifest` (same file, lines 64–67) filters every manifest entry through `isProjectPath` before returning it, so entries like `../secret.txt` or `C:\...` never make it into the in-memory manifest that `sync.ts` iterates over when deciding what to delete. It rejects a path if it's empty/non-string, absolute (`path.isAbsolute`), a drive-letter path (`/^[a-zA-Z]:/`), or if resolving it relative to `cwd` produces something outside `cwd` (`rel.startsWith("..")`). Since `sync()` (`src/commands/sync.ts:128-141`) only calls `rmSync` on paths that came from `entries` (built from `manifest?.files`), a manifest tampered with an out-of-project path is silently dropped rather than deleted.

dist/ is committed because agentos is often installed as a git dependency (`npm install -g <git-url>`), and under `-g` a nested npm install triggered by a build-type script inherits the outer `--global`/`--prefix` flags and corrupts the install tree. Since npm auto-runs `preinstall`, `install`, `postinstall`, `prepare`, `prepack`, or `build` scripts on install, none of those can exist — the compile step is deliberately named `compile` instead, and CI verifies dist/ stays in sync with source.

SCRIPTS: preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare, prepack, build

The function is `isProjectPath`, defined in `src/core/manifest.ts` (lines 42–46).

Mechanics:

1. `sync.ts`'s deletion loop (lines 128–141) only ever operates on entries that came from `readManifest(cwd)`.
2. `readManifest` filters the raw JSON's `files` array through `isProjectPath(cwd, f.path)` before returning it (manifest.ts:64–67) — so a tampered `../secret.txt` or `C:\...` entry never even survives parsing into an in-memory `ManifestEntry`.
3. `isProjectPath` rejects the entry if the path is absolute (`path.isAbsolute(p)`), Windows-drive-qualified (`/^[a-zA-Z]:/`), or if resolving it against `cwd` and taking the relative path yields something starting with `..` — i.e. it escapes the project root.

Since `entries` in `sync.ts` is built from `manifest?.files ?? []` (line 104), any malicious path is already gone before the `rmSync(abs)` call on line 134 ever runs, so sync can't be tricked into deleting a file outside the project.
